questionText:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) A company is an artificial person.
(B) Company's shares are generally transferable.
(C) Paid up capital can exceed called up capital.
(D) The part of capital which is called up only on winding up is called
reserve capital.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.quick: A company is an artificial person (A), shares are transferable (B), and reserve capital is called up only on winding up (D); paid up capital cannot exceed called up capital (C is false).
solution.concept:
According to NCERT Class 12 Accountancy Part 2, Chapter 1: Accounting for Share Capital, Section 1.2 and 1.3:
1. A company is an artificial legal person created by law with perpetual succession (A is true).
2. Shares of a public company are freely transferable (B is true).
3. Paid-up capital is that portion of called-up capital which is actually received from shareholders; it cannot exceed called-up capital (C is false).
4. Reserve capital is that portion of uncalled capital which a company decides by special resolution to call only in the event of winding up (Section 99 Companies Act 2013) (D is true).
solution.step_by_step:
1. Evaluate statement (A): Company is an artificial person - True.
2. Evaluate statement (B): Company shares are transferable - True.
3. Evaluate statement (C): Paid up capital exceeds called up - False (Paid up <= Called up).
4. Evaluate statement (D): Capital called only on winding up is reserve capital - True.
5. Valid statements: (A), (B) and (D) only, matching Option A.
solution.detailed:
1. Evaluate statement (A): Company is an artificial person - True.
2. Evaluate statement (B): Company shares are transferable - True.
3. Evaluate statement (C): Paid up capital exceeds called up - False (Paid up <= Called up).
4. Evaluate statement (D): Capital called only on winding up is reserve capital - True.
5. Valid statements: (A), (B) and (D) only, matching Option A.

questionText:
The assets of the firm, including any sum contributed by the partners to
make deficiencies of capital, shall be applied first for paying
…………………..

options.text: Each partner proportionately for any advances made to firm.
Debts of the firm to the third parties
Paying partners proportionately for their capital balances.
Partners in their profit sharing ratio.

solution.quick: Under Section 48(b)(i), firm assets are applied first in paying the debts of the firm to third parties.
solution.concept:
Section 48(b) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 mandates that upon dissolution, assets of the firm (including sums contributed by partners to make up deficiencies) shall be applied in the following order of priority:
1. First in paying the debts of the firm to third parties (outside liabilities).
2. Next in paying each partner rateably what is due for advances (loans).
3. Next in paying each partner rateably what is due on account of capital.
4. Lastly, the residue is divided among partners in profit-sharing ratio.
step_by_step: Step 1: Refer to Section 48(b) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
Step 2: The very first priority is discharging debts owed to outside third parties.
Step 3: Partner loans come second, partner capitals third, and residue fourth.
Step 4: Select option B.
detailed: Step 1: Refer to Section 48(b) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
Step 2: The very first priority is discharging debts owed to outside third parties.
Step 3: Partner loans come second, partner capitals third, and residue fourth.
Step 4: Select option B.

distractor_analysis.B: Correct. Debts of the firm to third parties are paid first under Section 48(b)(i).
distractor_analysis.C: Incorrect. Partner capital balances are paid third under Section 48(b)(iii).
distractor_analysis.D: Incorrect. Residual distribution in PSR is the final step under Section 48(b)(iv).
